title: Treadmill-based task for assessing spatial memory in head-fixed mice
protocol: Anesthetize the mouse in accordance with IACUC-approved protocols.
Maintain anesthesia with 1%–2% isoflurane and 0.5 L/min O2 on a heating pad.
Clean scalp with betadine and 70% ethanol.
Make a longitudinal incision about 5–6 mm long to expose the skull.
Thoroughly etch the surface of the skull to enhance bonding of Optibond and dental cement.
Apply a layer of Optibond dental adhesive over the exposed skull surface.
Cure the Optibond using blue light.
Sterilize grounding pin if necessary, then implant on the back of the skull over the cerebellum.
Prepare a smooth portion of the back of the skull by trimming neck muscle.
Carefully scrape away connective tissue where the muscle connects to the skull with a scalpel.
Drill a small (∼1 mm) craniotomy.
Insert the tungsten wire end of the gold pin into the craniotomy using forceps.
Apply Flow-It ALC around the base of the pin.
Cure the dental cement with blue light.
Implant the headbar using dental cement.
Apply a thin layer of dental cement over the entire surface of the skull.
Wait 2–3 minutes for the thin layer to set slightly.
Apply a small amount of thick dental cement to the back of the skull.
Place the headbar in the middle of the thick spot of cement immediately, ensuring wings are perpendicular to the mouse’s body long axis.
Balance the headbar before the cement fully dries.
Apply one last coat of dental cement over the back of the headbar and spread it carefully around the rest of the skull without covering the wings of the headbar.
Allow the dental cement 5–10 minutes to dry completely.
Mix 5 mg/kg of carpofen in saline at a concentration of 1 mg/mL.
Inject the mouse subcutaneously with the prepared carpofen solution.
Replace homecage water with 2% citric acid water.
Weigh mice prior to treatment (baseline).
Weigh mice every day for 5 days and then once per week after treatment begins.
Ensure animal weight does not drop below 85% of baseline weight.
If weight drops below threshold, provide immediate access to 1 mL clean water.
Remove from experiments if mouse continues to be below weight threshold.
Habituate mice to handling by the experimenter for at least 3 minutes per day for 3 days.
Ensure sufficient water in syringe before starting behavior sessions.
Run a test session to ensure all data are being acquired.
Begin with 20-min training sessions on the treadmill for mice.
Reduce training time by 5 min per session as mice improve their walking ability.
Continue training until sessions are 10 min long or mice meet experimental criteria.
Run the program RunTreadmill.m and enter relevant information in the GUI.
Do not start data acquisition until the mouse is head-fixed.
Affix the headbar to the head plate when ready.
Gently tug the treadmill belt if the mouse turns so that its rear legs are to the side or nearly in front of the head.
Take care not to stress mice when placing them on and off the treadmill.
Quickly transfer mice from the cage to the treadmill platform.
Avoid dangling mice by the tail during transfer.
Do not overly force the mouse into head-fixation.
Place the mouse behind the head-fixation stage initially.
Pull the belt forward lightly if the mouse ducks under the head-fixation stage.
Hold the headbar in place while screws are inserted for fixation.
Train animals to lick the reward spout by administering a free 10 μL reward at the beginning of each training session.
Touch the reward spout gently to the snout when initiating licking training.
Only train once per day for the first 2–3 days with initial rewards.
Start a timer for the duration of the training session from the MATLAB command line.
Unscrew the headbar and gently place the mouse back in the homecage at the end of the session.
Check performance on the task by running the OpenTreadmillFile.m program.
Mix 4 μL to 20 μL of reward as needed for experimental conditions.
Use a 10 μL reward volume for the experiment.
Clean the syringe containing sweetened water with 70% ethanol and tap water once per week.
Flush the syringe thoroughly to avoid mold growth.
Regularly clean the area around mouse feces to maintain hygiene.
Replace treadmill belts every 1 to 2 months based on frequency and volume of use.
